# Proposed code fix (not applied)

## Diagnosis
Stage 01 evaluator returned PASS. Stage 02 failed twice in driver.log/run.log: plan_tiles.py lines 114 and 125 concatenate concept ID, `#assessment:`, and the full capability. Six resulting references exceed common.schema.json's 160-character ID limit. This is a deterministic producer/representation bug, not an evaluator defect or transient outage. No working/sub_*.log files are present.

## Implementation description
Keep the existing schema limit and all evaluator, lineage, coverage, ledger and gate checks unchanged. Introduce a shared assessment-reference encoder and resolver in scripts/finlib.py:

* For a `(concept_id, capability)` pair, preserve the existing `concept_id#assessment:capability` encoding when it fits the 160-character limit.
* Otherwise encode as `ar.<sha256>` using the full SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical JSON array `[concept_id, capability]` (existing canon()/hashlib helpers). This is 67 characters and matches the existing ID pattern. Do not truncate capability text or change source glossary identifiers.
* Build a reverse index from every glossary assessment anchor's encoded reference to its original `(concept_id, capability)` and anchor object. Reject duplicate source pairs and any reference collision; reject unknown references instead of guessing. Resolve legacy references through this same index.
* Replace both assessment-reference comprehensions in plan_tiles.py (lines 114 and 125) with calls to that shared encoder. Keep practice/visual anchors unchanged.
* Update validate_tile.py's planned assessment loop (lines 253–257): identify assessment references through the reverse index rather than splitting every reference at '#'; resolve original concept and capability before comparing to interaction.measures. Preserve the current mismatch reporting and all independent coverage checks. An unknown assessment reference must be reported as an error, not silently skipped.
* Include the resolved original capability and concept alongside compact reference IDs in generator/evaluator input packets, so models can faithfully copy reference IDs while using unchanged full capabilities in measures. Update evaluator_packet.py line 198 to display compact references via the resolver rather than unconditionally calling a.split('#')[1]. Audit other consumers/templates of assessment references for the same assumption; do not substitute digest strings into measures.capability.

## Tests and resume
Add tests for short-reference backwards compatibility, all failing long references in this batch, deterministic encoding, round-trip resolution, unknown-reference rejection and collision detection. Verify stage 02 output and authored lineage against the unmodified schemas, and verify original capability coverage and planned-measure checks still work for compact references.
